lines.text: Unit 02 Spread of Islam
TranslationMovement
After the dawn of the Abbasid rule, translations from
Greek, Syriac, Persian and Sanskrit opened the doors
of knowledge for the Muslim world. Though this
translation movement had been started during
Umayyad period, it flourished during Abbasids time.
During the caliphate of Mamun al Rashid, the House
of Wisdom was turned into an institute of translation.
Texts on mathematics, astronomy, astrology and
medicine were translated over the years. This
translation movement played an important role in the
developmentofArabscientificknowledge.
Scientists and artists enjoyed freedom
MuslimScientists
of thought and action during Abbasid
Dynasty
The tenth and eleventh centuries AD witnessed many Muslim scholars who contributed
to the world of knowledge. Some of the best-known intellectuals of that time were
Al-Razi, Ibn Sina, Al-Khwarizmi, Al-Beruni and Jabir Bin Hayyan. There were many other
scientists too who played important role in spreading light of knowledge to the world.
AbuBakrMuhammad al-Razi(854-935AD)was a physician,
philosopher and chemist.Most of his works in medical field were
translated into Latin and circulated widely in Europe.He wrote
237 books butmostof them are extinct today.SirrAl-asrar
(Secret of Secrets) is Razi's most famous book which has gained
a lot of recognition.

Muhammad al-Razi
jurisprudence before engaging with geometry, logic, other
aspects of philosophy and medicine.Two of his most famous
works which survived are the Book of Healing [of the Soul], a
philosophical compendium, and the Canon of Medicine, a
comprehensivemedicalwork.
Al-Khwarizmi (750-825 AD),a mathematician and astronomer,
explained the use of zero and advanced the decimal system.He
introduced important mathematical terms like“algebra"and
"algorithm".Al-Khwarizmi is also known as father of Algebra.
Al-Khwarizmi
Abu Reyhan Muhammad Ibne Ahmed al-Beruni (973-1052) is considered as one of great
Muslim scientists till date. He wrote around 15o books, most of which were on
Mathematics and astronomy. His other works are on Physics, anthropology,
pharmacology, minerology and history. His compendium of India; "kitab al-Hind; Kitab
al-Birunif Tahqiq ma li-al-Hind" provides an insight of Indian philosophy and religion.
